```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE)
library(tidyverse)
library(lme4)
library(lmerTest)
```

# Data

Long-form feature listing data (one row per participant, cue, and feature word). All idiosyncratic responses are kept.

```{r load-data}
fl <- read_csv("../data/08_words.csv")
glimpse(fl)
```

```{r data-summary}
fl %>%
  summarise(
    participants = n_distinct(subject_id),
    cues = n_distinct(cue),
    features = n_distinct(word),
    rows = n()
  )
```

# Predictors

## Concreteness norms

Brysbaert et al. (2014) concreteness ratings (1 = abstract, 5 = concrete), joined to both cues and features.

```{r concreteness}
conc <- read_csv("../data/concreteness_norms.csv")

fl <- fl %>%
  left_join(conc %>% select(cue = word, cue_concrete = concreteness), by = "cue") %>%
  left_join(conc %>% select(word, feature_concrete = concreteness), by = "word")

fl %>%
  summarise(
    cue_coverage = mean(!is.na(cue_concrete)),
    feature_coverage = mean(!is.na(feature_concrete))
  )
```

## Feature frequency

Frequency of a feature within a cue (number of participants who listed it). Collocational frequency (for example from OpenSubtitles) is still TODO.

```{r frequency}
pairs <- fl %>%
  group_by(cue, word, cue_concrete, feature_concrete) %>%
  summarise(feature_frequency = n_distinct(subject_id), .groups = "drop") %>%
  filter(!is.na(cue_concrete), !is.na(feature_concrete))

nrow(pairs)
```

## Semantic distance (added to the cue-feature pairs)

Cue-feature distance from the Lancaster sensorimotor norms (Lynott et al., 2020): cosine distance (1 - cosine similarity) between the 11-dimension sensorimotor vectors of the cue and the feature. Words with an all-zero vector have no defined cosine and are dropped. Embedding-based distance is still TODO.

```{r sem-distance}
lanc <- read_csv("../data/lancaster_norms.csv")
lanc_mat <- lanc %>% select(-word) %>% as.matrix()
rownames(lanc_mat) <- lanc$word
lanc_mat <- lanc_mat[sqrt(rowSums(lanc_mat^2)) > 0, ]
lanc_unit <- lanc_mat / sqrt(rowSums(lanc_mat^2))

pairs <- pairs %>%
  filter(cue %in% rownames(lanc_unit), word %in% rownames(lanc_unit)) %>%
  mutate(sem_distance = 1 - rowSums(lanc_unit[cue, , drop = FALSE] * lanc_unit[word, , drop = FALSE]))

nrow(pairs)
summary(pairs$sem_distance)
```

# Cue concreteness vs. feature concreteness

Using features as Y and cues as X, we expect a strong correlation but also a higher intercept (Dunning-Kruger-like pattern?). Cue-level means avoid weighting cues by how many features they have.

```{r correlation}
cue_means <- pairs %>%
  group_by(cue, cue_concrete) %>%
  summarise(mean_feature_concrete = mean(feature_concrete),
            mean_feature_concrete_weighted = weighted.mean(feature_concrete, feature_frequency),
            .groups = "drop")

cor.test(cue_means$cue_concrete, cue_means$mean_feature_concrete)

m_cue <- lm(mean_feature_concrete ~ cue_concrete, data = cue_means)
summary(m_cue)

ggplot(cue_means, aes(cue_concrete, mean_feature_concrete)) +
  geom_point(alpha = .4) +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm") +
  geom_abline(slope = 1, intercept = 0, linetype = "dashed") +
  labs(x = "Cue concreteness", y = "Mean feature concreteness",
       caption = "Dashed line: feature = cue") +
  theme_minimal()
```

# Hierarchical mixed models

Feature concreteness is a property of the word, so it is constant across cues and people: a random intercept for feature word would absorb all of its variance and make the model degenerate. Only cue is random here. This is at the cue-feature pair level; participant-level data is still TODO.

Models are added in steps so each addition can be tested against the previous model (likelihood ratio tests on ML fits).

```{r hierarchical}
pairs <- pairs %>%
  mutate(z_dist = scale(sem_distance)[, 1],
         z_freq = scale(feature_frequency)[, 1])

m0 <- lmer(feature_concrete ~ 1 + (1 | cue), data = pairs, REML = FALSE)
m1 <- lmer(feature_concrete ~ cue_concrete + (1 | cue), data = pairs, REML = FALSE)
m2 <- update(m1, . ~ . + z_dist)
m3 <- update(m2, . ~ . + z_freq)
m4 <- update(m3, . ~ . + z_dist:z_freq)

anova(m0, m1, m2, m3, m4)
```

```{r fit-summary}
# marginal R2 (fixed effects) and conditional R2 (fixed + cue) for each step
r2 <- function(m) {
  vf <- var(as.vector(model.matrix(m) %*% fixef(m)))
  vc <- sum(as.data.frame(VarCorr(m))$vcov)
  c(marginal = vf / (vf + vc), conditional = (vf + VarCorr(m)$cue[1]) / (vf + vc))
}

step_names <- c("0 null", "1 + cue concreteness", "2 + semantic distance",
                "3 + feature frequency", "4 + distance x frequency")
models <- list(m0, m1, m2, m3, m4)

fit_table <- tibble(
  step = step_names,
  AIC = map_dbl(models, AIC),
  BIC = map_dbl(models, BIC),
  R2_marginal = map_dbl(models, ~ r2(.x)["marginal"]),
  R2_conditional = map_dbl(models, ~ r2(.x)["conditional"])
) %>%
  mutate(delta_R2_marginal = R2_marginal - lag(R2_marginal))

fit_table
```

```{r final-model}
summary(m4)
```

# Participant-level models

The same hierarchy on the full long-form data (one row per participant, cue, and feature), adding a random intercept for participant. Pair-level frequency and distance are joined back onto each row.

```{r participant-data}
pl <- fl %>%
  inner_join(pairs %>% select(cue, word, sem_distance, feature_frequency, z_dist, z_freq),
             by = c("cue", "word"))
nrow(pl)
```

```{r participant-models}
p1 <- lmer(feature_concrete ~ cue_concrete + (1 | cue) + (1 | subject_id), data = pl, REML = FALSE)
p2 <- update(p1, . ~ . + z_dist)
p3 <- update(p2, . ~ . + z_freq)
p4 <- update(p3, . ~ . + z_dist:z_freq)

anova(p1, p2, p3, p4)
summary(p4)
```

The planned structure was `(participant | cue)`; adjust the random effects if the model fails to converge.
